text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- South Africa, probing allegations of abuse of the Duty Credit Certificate Scheme within the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), said it would work towards changing customs regulations if allegations of illicit deals between Namibian and South African companies were confirmed.
- President Sam Nujoma has yet to finalise actions he intends to take to deal with allegations of an illegal seal meat operation at Henties Bay.
- The environment and tourism ministry said it would take new measures to protect the fragile environment around Sesriem and Sossusvlei against an onslaught of tourists.
- A committee appointed to coordinate water supply to the central regions of the country has found that water stored in supply dams was secure for the next three years.

- The DTA's shadow agriculture minister Andries Mouton has called for legislation to protect farmers against cheap, subsidised meat from the EU and Australia which is being dumped on the local market via South Africa.
